first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the 4% completion decline and may also recover activation by accelerating time-to-value. Two inherited findings support this direction, while promotional pricing carries a documented 30-day retention penalty that conflicts with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Verification is still required before final commitment.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening the onboarding flow. The verified onboarding source directly matches the current completion decline and improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%. The verified SMB signup result also supports simplification as an activation lever, though its 1% retention decline warrants explicit retention guardrails. Promotional pricing is not selected because its documented retention harm conflicts with sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

final2.rationale: Reallocate the single experiment to narrowly targeted promotional pricing for price-sensitive SMB accounts showing churn risk. The doubled churn conversations and deeper competitor cut make price response the most immediate qualified-revenue defense. Keep the test small because prior evidence showed strong acquisition and revenue lift but materially worse 30-day retention; use strict eligibility, limited duration, and retention and qualified-revenue guardrails rather than generalizing the offer.
